description: Convert a document to another format without storing a template. Pure conversion: no data is sent, so Carbone tags such as {d.name} are kept as written; this is also how you proof a template in another format (DOCX template → PDF, or DOCX → ODT while it stays a template). The source file can be a local file path, an HTTPS URL, or a base64-encoded string. Use render_document instead when you need data injection ({d.field} tags resolved), translations, or batch generation. Example: { "file": "/Users/me/report.docx", "convertTo": "pdf" } (a bare file name such as "report.docx" is not a path). Common conversions: DOCX → PDF (add converter: "I" for the fastest conversion), XLSX → PDF, PPTX → PDF, HTML → PDF (converter: "C" for full CSS/JS rendering), DOCX → HTML, XLSX → CSV, PDF → PNG, PPTX → PNG (first slide as image), MD → PDF.

asAttachment.description: If true, return the document as a downloadable file attachment (a base64 EmbeddedResource), for any format. Default delivery: text and png/jpg/gif/webp are returned inline; other binary outputs (PDF, Office, …) are saved to a temp file (path returned). Ignored when outputPath or returnLink is set.

formatOptions.description: Format-specific options. Examples: PDF password: { "EncryptFile": true, "DocumentOpenPassword": "s3cr3t" }; PDF permissions: { "RestrictPermissions": true, "PermissionPassword": "owner" }; PDF watermarks (max 4): { "Watermarks": [{ "text": "DRAFT", "size": 60, "opacity": 0.2, "rotation": -45 }] }; PDF/A (L only): { "SelectPdfVersion": 2 } (2 = PDF/A-2b, 3 = PDF/A-3b, 4 = PDF/A-4); page selection (L only): { "PageRange": "1-5" }; accessibility (L only): { "UseTaggedPDF": true, "PDFUACompliance": true }; JPG/PNG: { "PixelWidth": 1200, "PixelHeight": 630 }, JPG quality: { "Quality": 80 } (1-100); CSV: { "fieldSeparator": ";" }. All options: https://carbone.io/documentation/developer/http-api/generate-reports.html#pdf-options

convertTo.description: Target output format. Valid outputs depend on the input format (e.g. HTML converts to pdf, docx or png, but not xlsx); see the conversion matrix: https://carbone.io/documentation/developer/http-api/generate-reports.html#output-file-type. "doc", "xls" and "ppt" are output formats; as input, use DOCX, XLSX or PPTX. Simple usage: "pdf". With options: { "formatName": "pdf", "formatOptions": { ... } }.

converter.description: Converter engine, used whenever the format changes (not only for PDF). If omitted, "L" is used. "L" LibreOffice: DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODT, ODS, ODP, ODG, MD, PDF; the only converter supporting all PDF options. "I" Carbone ICE: DOCX and ODT to PDF; Carbone's own engine, 3x to 300x faster, recommended over "O" for DOCX from v5.15.0. It converts all content except WEBP and EMF/WMF images, SmartArt and complex charts (bar, line, area, pie and doughnut charts are drawn), comments, tracked changes, form fields and equations: keep the default "L" for documents with those. A missing font is replaced by Noto Sans (https://carbone.io/documentation/developer/http-api/generate-reports.html#converters-carbone-ice-limitations). "O" OnlyOffice: DOCX, XLSX, PPTX to PDF. "C" Chromium: HTML to PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP with full CSS/JS; 100 MB max. PDF options: "L" supports all of them; "O", "C" and "I" apply Security (passwords, permissions) and Watermarks. Docs: https://carbone.io/documentation/developer/http-api/generate-reports.html#converters

egressAuthorization.description: Value for the Authorization header Carbone adds to its OUTBOUND (egress) requests during conversion — e.g. when a Chromium HTML→PDF conversion fetches a protected external image or stylesheet. For example "Bearer abc123" makes Carbone send `authorization: Bearer abc123` to those hosts. Only the authorization header can be customised; max 511 characters.

file.description: The document to convert. Three input forms are accepted: (1) Local file path — absolute, e.g. "/Users/me/report.docx" (or "C:\Users\me\report.docx" on Windows), or under the home directory, e.g. "~/report.docx". A relative path must start with "./" or "../" and resolves against the server process's working directory, which is rarely yours: prefer an absolute path. A bare file name such as "report.docx" is NOT a path: it would be sent as base64 content. (2) HTTPS URL — the file is downloaded automatically, e.g. "https://example.com/file.pptx". (3) Base64-encoded string — the raw file content encoded as base64. Supported input formats: DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODT, ODS, ODP, ODG, HTML, XHTML, XML, SVG, IDML, MD, TXT, CSV, RTF, PDF. Carbone reads XML-based and text-based documents (plus PDF): the legacy binary Office formats DOC, XLS and PPT are rejected as input, although they are valid outputs. Re-save such a file as DOCX, XLSX or PPTX first. Full conversion matrix: https://carbone.io/documentation/developer/http-api/generate-reports.html#output-file-type

hardRefresh.description: If true, Carbone runs the converter even when the output format equals the input format, and recomputes pagination and the table of contents at the end of the conversion. Needed for PDF → PDF: without it Carbone returns the PDF unchanged and formatOptions (password, permissions, watermarks, PDF/A, …) are NOT applied. This server sets it automatically when the input is a PDF, convertTo is "pdf" and formatOptions are given; pass false to opt out. Example (PDF → PDF/A-4): { "hardRefresh": true, "convertTo": { "formatName": "pdf", "formatOptions": { "SelectPdfVersion": 4 } } }.

outputPath.description: Optional local file path to save the converted document to (e.g. "/home/user/out.pdf" or "~/out.pdf"). When set, the file is written to disk and the tool returns the saved path + size instead of embedding the document inline — ideal for large files. The path must not exist yet: an existing file is never overwritten (the call fails and asks for a new file name).

reportName.description: Name of the delivered file, WITHOUT extension (e.g. "contract", "2026-invoice"). The document is delivered as "<reportName>.<ext>", with the extension of convertTo, used as the attachment name and the default saved file name. This server names the file itself: a conversion has no templating pass, which is where Carbone resolves reportName. Used literally: Carbone tags such as {d.id} are not resolved here. Ignored with returnLink (a download URL, not a named file) and with outputPath (which sets the path itself).

returnLink.description: If true, generate the document and return a public download URL instead of the file contents. The link is SHORT-LIVED and ONE-TIME — Carbone deletes the file after the first download — so it is meant for the end user to download once (do not fetch it programmatically). Works in stdio and HTTP. Mutually exclusive with outputPath and asAttachment.
